# ↪️ Pull Request

```json
{ "source": ["a.html", "b.html"] }
```

issue_context.title: An array `package.json#source` should build these specified entries.
issue_context.body:
Running `parcel build my-package/` should build `a.html, b.html` if `my-package/package.json` contains:
```json
{
  "source": ["a.html", "b.html"]
}
```

So be equivalent to `cd my-package && parcel build a.html b.html`.


The docs already say this should work: https://v2.parceljs.org/configuration/package-json/#source

Relevant code:
https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/064ba0a166ea63ccd2b623dc11324d4cd7ffb526/packages/core/core/src/requests/EntryRequest.js#L98-L126
comments: @mischnic I'd love to pick this issue up.
@mischnic how do you run build if there's a source file `{"source": "src/index.js"}` in your package.json for instance?

Pass the directory which contains the package.json as an argument:

> Running `parcel build my-package/` should build `a.html, b.html` if `my-package/package.json` contains:

(or `parcel build .` if the cwd is `my-package` already)
@mischnic I keep getting an error that says "no entries found" when I run the above command why?
@mischnic, please review this pull request, so that I can pick up a new issue and work on it.
You can also work on something else even before you PR is merged, if you want.

review_comments: @mischnic is this semantically correct? If pkg.source is an array then there will be the same { filePath: pkg.filePath } pushed for every source? seems like only a single one should be pushed.
